t: At-home telemedicine controlled taVNS twice daily for 4 weeks reduces long COVID symptoms of anxiety and fatigue
Non-invasive brain microcurrent stimulation therapy of long-COVID-19 reduces vascular dysregulation and improves visual and cognitive impairment.
Investigating the relationship between physical activity and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
f: Thesis: meta-analysis found pooled peak VO2 lower in ME/CFS than healthy controls (pooled difference about 5.2 ml/kg/min); also examines physical activity and exercise interventions.
nt: Thesis abstract truncated; effect size read from partial text

t: COVID-19 and post-infectious myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: a narrative review.
Beyond bones: The relevance of variants of connective tissue (hypermobility) to fibromyalgia, ME/CFS and controversies surrounding diagnostic classification: an observational study.
f: 81% of FM/ME-CFS patients met Brighton hypermobility criteria (OR 7.08) and 18% met 2017 hEDS criteria.

t: Comparison of the finger plethysmography derived stroke volumes by Nexfin CO Trek and suprasternal aortic Doppler derived stroke volume measurements in adults with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and in healthy controls.
f: Nexfin CO Trek finger plethysmography overestimates stroke volume vs suprasternal Doppler during tilt; calibration to Doppler makes it usable.

t: [Asthenic disorders as a manifestation of chronic fatigue syndrome].
f: Russian review of asthenic disorders as CFS with a suggestion that the peptide drug cortexin could be used.

t: Adaptation and validation of the Health Anxiety Inventory (short version) for medical settings
f: Adaptation and validation of a health anxiety inventory for medical settings, tested in MS, ME/CFS and chronic pain.

t: [Chronic fatigue syndrome against the background of the COVID-19 pandemic].
f: Russian review of possible post-COVID chronic fatigue syndrome causes and treatment.

t: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Organic Disease or Psychosomatic Illness? A Re-Examination of the Royal Free Epidemic of 1955.
f: Accounts from Royal Free staff of the 1955 outbreak were typical of an infectious illness, arguing against epidemic hysteria.

t: A Literature Review of GP Knowledge and Understanding of ME/CFS: A Report from the Socioeconomic Working Group of the European Network on ME/CFS (EUROMENE).
f: Literature review: a third to a half of GPs did not accept ME/CFS as a genuine entity and many lacked diagnostic confidence.

t: Correction to: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials for chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME).
Post-COVID-19 Fatigue: Potential Contributing Factors.
f: Perspective proposing a model of central, psychological and peripheral contributors to post-COVID fatigue.

t: Post-COVID-19 fatigue and anhedonia: A cross-sectional study and their correlation to post-recovery period.
f: Post-COVID patients had high fatigue and anhedonia scores that correlated with each other and with time since recovery.

t: COVID-19 related fatigue: Which role for rehabilitation in post-COVID-19 patients? A case series.
Updated NICE guidance on chronic fatigue syndrome.
Measuring improvement and deterioration in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: the pitfalls of the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire.
The Prospects of the Two-Day Cardiopulmonary Exercise Test (CPET) in ME/CFS Patients: A Meta-Analysis.
Potential causal factors of CFS/ME: a concise and systematic scoping review of factors researched.
f: Scoping review of causal-factor research: immunological (297), psychological (243), infection (198), neuroendocrine (198); most studies case-control, over half n<=100.

t: Fungal Dysbiosis Correlates with the Development of Tumor-Induced Cachexia in Mice.
f: Gut fungal dysbiosis in tumour-induced cachexia in mice; ME only mentioned as a comparator.

t: Could Cognitive Behavioural Therapy Be an Effective Treatment for Long COVID and Post COVID-19 Fatigue Syndrome? Lessons from the Qure Study for Q-Fever Fatigue Syndrome.
Paediatric chronic fatigue syndrome: 25 year perspective.
Long-Haul COVID-19: Putative Pathophysiology, Risk Factors, and Treatments
f: Narrative review of long-haul COVID pathophysiology, risk factors (female sex, early dyspnea, D-dimer) and treatments.

t: [Chronic fatigue syndrome: source of controversy].
Understanding the economic impact of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome in Ireland: a qualitative study.
f: Focus groups in Ireland described healthcare barriers, socioeconomic and disability-related costs.

t: Advances in Clinical Research on Traditional Chinese Medicine Treatment of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
Elevated Perceived Exertion in People with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Fibromyalgia: A Meta-analysis.
f: Perceived exertion during aerobic exercise higher in ME/CFS and FM than controls (Hedges d 0.85, 95% CI 0.62-1.08).
n: 37 studies, 1016 patients vs 686 controls (ME/CFS and FM)

t: Patients' experiences and effects of non-pharmacological treatment for myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome - a scoping mixed methods review.
f: Scoping review of European non-pharmacological therapies: CBT reduced fatigue more than usual care; rehabilitation and pacing results inconsistent.

t: Perfectionism, depression and anxiety in chronic fatigue syndrome: A systematic review.
f: Maladaptive perfectionism was consistently associated with depression in CFS/ME (r 0.42-0.48).

t: A Literature Review of GP Knowledge and Understanding of ME/CFS: A Report from the Socioeconomics Working Group of the European Network on ME/CFS (EUROMENE)
When is it safe to return to exercise post-COVID-19?
Autonomic dysfunction in 'long COVID': rationale, physiology and management strategies.
Multi-omics examination of Q fever fatigue syndrome identifies similarities with chronic fatigue syndrome.
Involvement of Cervical Muscle Lesions and Autonomic Nervous System in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis / Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)
f: Daily physical therapy to cervical muscles in hospital reported 55.5% recovery of ME/CFS by self-rating; pupil diameter used for autonomic function.
nt: Uncontrolled, self-rated, single Japanese centre, preprint

t: Role of mitochondria, oxidative stress and the response to antioxidants in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: A possible approach to SARS-CoV-2 'long-haulers'?
Informatics Inference of Exercise-Induced Modulation of Brain Pathways Based on Cerebrospinal Fluid Micro-RNAs in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: CSF miRNAs miR-608, -328, -200a-5p, -93-3p, -92a-3p were lower after submaximal exercise, implying altered phosphoinositol signalling and adhesion pathways.
nt: Different groups for rest and exercise; informatics inference

t: Impact of Long-Term Cryopreservation on Blood Immune Cell Markers in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Implications for Biomarker Discovery.
f: Biobanked frozen PBMCs showed no Treg or NK subset differences between ME/CFS and controls, and cryopreservation altered NK markers (CD25, CD69, NKp46).
nt: Small; methodological caution for biobank immune markers

t: Towards personalized assessment of fatigue perpetuating factors in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome using ecological momentary assessment: A pilot study.
f: Ecological momentary assessment showed heterogeneous fatigue perpetuators across individuals; none predicted CBT outcome.

t: Deep phenotyping of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome in Japanese population.
A hierarchical logistic regression predicting rapid respiratory rates from post-exertional malaise.
f: Rapid resting respiratory rate was predicted by PEM, not psychological or sedentary measures.

t: Fibromyalgia and Chronic Fatigue Syndrome in the Age of COVID-19.
Profile of circulating microRNAs in myalgic encephalomyelitis and their relation to symptom severity, and disease pathophysiology.
f: Eleven circulating microRNAs differed in severely ill ME/CFS before and after a PEM-inducing stress challenge and related to symptom severity.

t: Sick of the Sick Role: Narratives of What "Recovery" Means to People With CFS/ME.
Accurate and objective determination of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome disease severity with a wearable sensor.
f: Wearable IMU 'UpTime' separated severity: severe under 20% of day upright, moderate 20-30%, controls over 30%.

t: Changes in DNA methylation profiles of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome patients reflect systemic dysfunctions.
Long COVID: don't consign ME/CFS to history.
Pressure Point Thresholds and ME/CFS Comorbidity as Indicators of Patient's Response to Manual Physiotherapy in Fibromyalgia.
f: In fibromyalgia manual physiotherapy, patients with comorbid ME/CFS responded less than FM-only patients; baseline pain threshold predicted response.

t: Effect of disease duration in a randomized Phase III trial of rintatolimod, an immune modulator for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: Post-hoc analysis of Phase III rintatolimod trial: patients with 2-8 years' illness had over twice the placebo-adjusted treadmill gain; 51.2% improved exercise duration by 25% or more (p=0.003); no response in >8 years.

t: Systematic Review of Primary Outcome Measurements for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome/Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME) in Randomized Controlled Trials.
f: Review of primary outcomes in CFS/ME RCTs: 96% used patient-reported measures (SF-36, CIS, Chalder most common).

t: Correction to: A systematic review of mitochondrial abnormalities in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome/systemic exertion intolerance disease.
Early Growth Response Gene Upregulation in Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV)-Associated Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS).
Prediction of Discontinuation of Structured Exercise Programme in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Patients.
f: Fukuda CFS patients with higher sympathetic vascular drive, slower reaction time and lower HRmax were less likely to complete a 16-week structured exercise programme; 35 discontinued.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis in children aged 5 to 11 years: A qualitative study.
f: Interviews on paediatric CFS/ME aged 5-11 described complex disability and differing parental roles by child age.

t: The Lonely, Isolating, and Alienating Implications of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
Cardiac Dimensions and Function Are Not Altered among Females with the Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: Echocardiographic cardiac dimensions and function (including strain) did not differ between ME/CFS and controls at rest.

t: Oxidative stress caused by a dysregulated Wnt/β-catenin signalling pathway is involved in abnormal placenta formation in pregnant mice with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: In a stress-induced CFS mouse model, pregnancy showed abnormal placenta, oxidative stress and inhibited Wnt/beta-catenin signalling.
nt: Mouse stress model of CFS; validity uncertain

t: Extracting medication information from unstructured public health data: a demonstration on data from population-based and tertiary-based samples.
f: NLP framework to extract and classify medication data from ME/CFS study free text.

t: Cytokine profiling of extracellular vesicles isolated from plasma in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: a pilot study.
f: Plasma EVs 30-130 nm were more abundant in ME/CFS; EV and plasma cytokine profiles examined by 45-plex assay.

t: Reductions in Cerebral Blood Flow Can Be Provoked by Sitting in Severe Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Patients.
f: Sitting for an hour reduced cerebral blood flow in severe ME/CFS (474 vs 627 mL/min in controls); 90 patients with orthostatic intolerance had -26.9% CBF reduction; supine CBF normal.
nt: Extends tilt-based CBF finding to bed-bound patients using milder sitting stress

t: DNA Methylation and Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor Expression Account for Symptoms and Widespread Hyperalgesia in Patients With Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Comorbid Fibromyalgia.
f: Serum BDNF higher and BDNF exon 9 methylation lower in CFS with fibromyalgia, with methylation predicting BDNF and symptoms.
nt: Comorbid FM; small; methylation findings historically poorly replicated

t: Resting-state functional connectivity, cognition, and fatigue in response to cognitive exertion: a novel study in adolescents with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Cognitive exertion lowered DMN connectivity and raised fatigue similarly in CFS/ME and controls; patients had higher baseline fatigue and poorer cognition.

t: [Scraping on head and face combined with stepping technique of tuina along lower limbs for chronic fatigue syndrome].
Processing of Laser-Evoked Potentials in Patients with Chronic Whiplash-Associated Disorders, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, and Healthy Controls: A Case-Control Study.
f: Laser-evoked potentials in CFS did not differ from controls, arguing against generalised nociceptive CNS hyperexcitability.

t: Recommendations for Epidemiological Research in ME/CFS from the EUROMENE Epidemiology Working Group
f: EUROMENE recommendations for standardising epidemiological data collection in ME/CFS.

t: The illness-disease dichotomy and the biological-clinical splitting of medicine.
f: Philosophical commentary on the illness-disease distinction using CFS as example.

t: A SWATH-MS analysis of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome peripheral blood mononuclear cell proteomes reveals mitochondrial dysfunction.
f: PBMC SWATH-MS proteomics: 9 of 11 patients separated from controls by PCA; 60 differentially expressed proteins pointing to deficient ATP production and oxidative stress.
nt: Very small; subgroup selected post hoc

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia-like symptoms are an integral component of the phenome of schizophrenia: neuro-immune and opioid system correlates.
f: Fibromyalgia/CFS-like symptoms in schizophrenia correlate with IL-6, HMGB1 and opioid markers.

t: How common are depression and anxiety in adolescents with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) and how should we screen for these mental health co-morbidities? A clinical cohort study.
f: 35% of adolescents with CFS/ME met criteria for a mental health disorder (20% depression, 27% anxiety); questionnaires moderately accurate.

t: Effectiveness a herbal medicine (Sipjeondaebo-tang) on adults with chronic fatigue syndrome: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
Post COVID-19 syndrome associated with orthostatic cerebral hypoperfusion syndrome, small fiber neuropathy and benefit of immunotherapy: a case report.
Characterization of Post-exertional Malaise in Patients With Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: Patients described variable PEM symptoms in daily life and after CPET, with core themes of exhaustion, cognitive difficulty and neuromuscular complaints.

t: Corrigendum: Neuroinflammation and Cytokines in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS): A Critical Review of Research Methods.
A relational analysis of an invisible illness: A meta-ethnography of people with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME) and their support needs.
f: Meta-ethnography of qualitative literature on support needs, framing invisibility, loss of self and fraught clinical encounters.

t: Cognitive behavioural therapy for chronic fatigue and chronic fatigue syndrome: outcomes from a specialist clinic in the UK.
f: Naturalistic CBT clinic: fatigue and function improved (d 0.45-0.91) and 85% self-reported improvement.
nt: Uncontrolled, self-report, includes chronic fatigue without ME/CFS

t: Pressure Point Threshold and ME/CFS comorbidity as Indicators of Physiotherapy Response in Fibromyalgia
f: Preprint version of FM manual physiotherapy study: patients with comorbid ME/CFS responded less than FM-only patients.

t: Orthostatic stress testing in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome patients with or without concomitant fibromyalgia: effects on pressure pain thresholds and temporal summation.
f: Head-up tilt lowered pressure pain thresholds in ME/CFS with or without FM but not in controls; windup higher than controls, unchanged by tilt.
nt: Orthostatic stress as a hyperalgesia trigger, like exercise

t: Using Plasma Autoantibodies of Central Nervous System Proteins to Distinguish Veterans with Gulf War Illness from Healthy and Symptomatic Controls.
f: CNS autoantibodies were elevated in Gulf War illness compared with healthy veterans, ME/CFS and IBS; ME/CFS used as symptomatic comparator.
n: 171 GWI vs 60 vs 50 ME/CFS vs 35 IBS

t: A botanical product containing cistanche and ginkgo extracts improves chronic fatigue syndrome: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
f: Cistanche plus ginkgo botanical for 60 days reduced Chalder fatigue, memory and PEM symptom scores and lowered blood ammonia and lactate versus placebo.
nt: Chinese CFS criteria likely not PEM-defined; preprint; self-report

t: Neuroimaging characteristics of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS): a systematic review.
Genetic risk factors of ME/CFS: a critical review.
Striking the balance with epistemic injustice in healthcare: the case of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome/Myalgic Encephalomyelitis.
f: Philosophical paper on epistemic injustice in healthcare using ME/CFS as a case.

t: An analysis of 2-day cardiopulmonary exercise testing to assess unexplained fatigue.
f: Two-day CPET repeatability in Gulf War illness: ICC at peak 0.84, smallest real difference about 19%, and no group-by-time interaction.
nt: Gulf War illness, not ME/CFS; small

t: Acupuncture of the Beishu acupoint participates in regulatory effects of ginsenoside Rg1 on T cell subsets of rats with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Acupuncture plus ginsenoside Rg1 improved swimming endurance and T cell subsets in a rat chronic-stress fatigue model.

t: Using structural and functional MRI as a neuroimaging technique to investigate chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalopathy: a systematic review.
f: Systematic review of structural and functional MRI: inconsistent anatomical differences, more or broader activation on tasks; insufficient data for a neural biomarker.

t: Signs of Intracranial Hypertension, Hypermobility, and Craniocervical Obstructions in Patients With Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
Fatigue-Related Cognitive-Behavioral Factors in Survivors of Childhood Cancer: Comparison with Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Survivors of Adult-Onset Cancer.
f: Cognitive-behavioural fatigue-maintaining factors overlapped substantially between childhood cancer survivors and CFS patients.
n: 34 childhood cancer survivors, 102 CFS, 95 adult cancer survivors

t: Discriminatory cytokine profiles predict muscle function, fatigue and cognitive function in patients with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)
f: Multivariate plasma and muscle cytokine profiles predicted diagnosis, maximal voluntary contraction, fatigue and cognitive reaction times, with little muscle mitochondrial dysfunction.

t: The Economic Impacts of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome in an Australian Cohort.
f: Australian cost-of-illness: estimated annual health-care and income-loss cost of AUD 14.5 billion; about 12 GP visits per participant per year.

t: Activity measurement in pediatric chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Actigraphy showed lower daytime activity, higher night-time activity and delayed daytime start in children with ME/CFS; self-report correlated with ActiGraph.

t: Hemodynamics during the 10-minute NASA Lean Test: evidence of circulatory decompensation in a subset of ME/CFS patients.

Validation of the Severity of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome by Other Measures than History: Activity Bracelet, Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing and a Validated Activity Questionnaire: SF-36.
f: ICC clinical severity grades tracked SF-36 physical function (70/43/15), steps/day (8235/5195/2031) and CPET ventilatory-threshold VO2 across mild/moderate/severe.

t: Recruiting Adolescents With Chronic Fatigue Syndrome/Myalgic Encephalomyelitis to Internet-Delivered Therapy: Internal Pilot Within a Randomized Controlled Trial.
f: Internal pilot of a trial of internet-delivered CBT (FITNET-NHS) for adolescents with CFS/ME assessing recruitment feasibility.

t: How Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) Progresses: The Natural History of ME/CFS.
f: Framework for ME/CFS natural history from predisposition through prodrome to a late hypometabolic state, with a hypermetabolic early neuro-immune phase.

t: Exercise alters brain activation in Gulf War Illness and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: Exercise changed N-back fMRI activation in ME/CFS (increased midbrain, operculo-insular and insula) but not controls; GWI showed deactivation, separating the two illnesses.

t: Environmental, Neuro-immune, and Neuro-oxidative Stress Interactions in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
Autonomic Phenotypes in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS) Are Associated with Illness Severity: A Cluster Analysis.
f: Cluster analysis of autonomic function (Fukuda CFS) gave four profiles; sympathetic-dysautonomia phenotype (34%) had more severe disease and lowest quality of life.

t: Effects of the prolong life with nine turn method (Yan Nian Jiu Zhuan) Qigong on patients with chronic fatigue syndrome: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
[Effect of ginger-separated moxibustion on fatigue, sleep quality and depression in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome: a randomized controlled trial].
Dental Care of the Homebound Patient with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/chronic Fatigue Syndrome
f: Considerations for dental care of homebound ME/CFS patients.

t: Mapping of pathological change in chronic fatigue syndrome using the ratio of T1- and T2-weighted MRI scans.
f: T1w/T2w MRI ratio raised in white matter, subcortical grey matter and brainstem in Fukuda ME/CFS; related to HRV, cognition and respiration rate.

t: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Efficacy of Repeat Immunoadsorption.
Review of case definitions for myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS).
A systematic review of mitochondrial abnormalities in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome/systemic exertion intolerance disease.
f: Systematic review of mitochondrial abnormalities found inconsistent results across structure, function, metabolites and coenzymes.

t: Commentary: Antibodies to Human Herpesviruses in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Patients.
Plasma proteomic profiling suggests an association between antigen driven clonal B cell expansion and ME/CFS.
f: Plasma proteomics associated IGHV3-23/30 with ME/CFS, suggesting antigen-driven B-cell clonal expansion; ML panels AUC 0.77-0.84.

t: Associations of physical and psychiatric conditions with chronic fatigue syndrome in Germany: an exploratory case-control study.
f: German primary-care CFS diagnoses associated with cancer (OR 2.57), sleep disorders (OR 1.88) and depression (OR 1.77).

t: Autoantibodies to beta-adrenergic and muscarinic cholinergic receptors in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME) patients - A validation study in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid from two Swedish cohorts.
Machine Learning Detects Pattern of Differences in Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) Data between Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS) and Gulf War Illness (GWI).
f: Machine learning on N-back fMRI before and after exercise separated CFS from Gulf War illness at about 75-79% accuracy.
nt: No healthy control comparison of classifier; modest sample

t: Severe ME in Children.
Health Care Responsibility and Compassion-Visiting the Housebound Patient Severely Affected by ME/CFS.
f: Opinion on providing compassionate home care for severely affected, housebound ME/CFS patients.

t: Altered Structural Brain Networks Related to Adrenergic/Muscarinic Receptor Autoantibodies in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: In ME/CFS, titers of beta1/beta2 adrenergic receptor autoantibodies correlated with local structural network measures in right prefrontal and precentral regions.
nt: No control group in abstract; weak regional correlations

t: Two-Day Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing in Females with a Severe Grade of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Comparison with Patients with Mild and Moderate Disease.
Preliminary ICF core set for patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome in rehabilitation medicine.
f: Preliminary ICF core set: 82-100% had impairments in energy, fatigue, endurance, sleep and pain; half had cognitive and sensory problems.

t: FUNGAL DYSBIOSIS CORRELATES WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF TUMOUR-INDUCED CACHEXIA IN MICE
f: Preprint of gut fungal dysbiosis in tumour cachexia in mice; ME only as comparator.

t: A concerning display of medical indifference: reply to 'Chronic fatigue syndrome and an illness-focused approach to care: controversy, morality and paradox'.
f: Commentary arguing ME/CFS should be treated as biomedical disease, replying to Sharpe and Greco.

t: Cognitive Function Declines Following Orthostatic Stress in Adults With Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS).
f: N-back working memory worsened after 30-min head-up tilt (2-back correct 77% to 62%, 3-back 57% to 41%) in ME/CFS.

t: How to support the quality of life of people living with cognitive disorders: a (k)new challenge in the post-COVID-19 world.
Epidemiological and clinical factors associated with post-exertional malaise severity in patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: PEM severity associated with onset age 32 or older (OR 1.8), recurrent infections (OR 2.1) and certain precipitants in ICC patients.

t: The effectiveness of cupping therapy on chronic fatigue syndrome: A single-blind randomized controlled trial.
Predictors of new onsets of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia: the lifelines study.
f: Dutch population cohort: new-onset CFS predictors were mostly syndrome-specific, and CFS was more distinct from IBS and FM.

t: Cerebral Blood Flow Is Reduced in Severe Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Patients During Mild Orthostatic Stress Testing: An Exploratory Study at 20 Degrees of Head-Up Tilt Testing.
f: In severe ME/CFS, a 15-min 20-degree tilt reduced cerebral blood flow by 27%, comparable to the 26% decline with 70-degree tilt in milder patients.

t: Risk factors for suicide in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Archival data: suicide risk higher in those using the CFS label, with limited function and without comorbid illness.

t: Review of the Quality Control Checks Performed by Current Genome-Wide and Targeted-Genome Association Studies on Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
The Relationship Between Childhood Trauma and the Response to Group Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: Childhood trauma did not predict response to group CBT for CDC-defined CFS.

t: Predicting GP visits: A multinomial logistic regression investigating GP visits amongst a cohort of UK patients living with Myalgic encephalomyelitis.
f: UK ME patient survey: illness duration, trust in GP, diagnosis time and sex predicted GP visits.

t: "The child's got a complete circle around him". The care of younger children (5-11 years) with CFS/ME. A qualitative study comparing families', teachers' and clinicians' perspectives'.

Physical activity measures in patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: correlations between peak oxygen consumption, the physical functioning scale of the SF-36 questionnaire, and the number of steps from an activity meter.
f: SF-36 physical function, steps/day and %peak VO2 were significantly correlated in ME/CFS; single measures inadequate.

t: Protective Effect of Hemin Against Experimental Chronic Fatigue Syndrome in Mice: Possible Role of Neurotransmitters.
f: Hemin improved behaviour, oxidative stress and neurotransmitters in a mouse forced-swim fatigue model.

t: Health-related quality of life in Norwegian adolescents living with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Norwegian adolescents with CFS/ME had low quality of life (PedsQL 50), lower in girls; school support associated with better scores.

t: The concept of 'illness without disease' impedes understanding of chronic fatigue syndrome: a response to Sharpe and Greco.
f: Response arguing against labelling ME/CFS as 'illness without disease'.

t: Clinical History Segment Extraction from Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Assessments to Model Disease Trajectories.
f: NLP method to extract clinical history segments from CFS assessments.

t: Mitochondria and immunity in chronic fatigue syndrome.
Letter to the Editor of Metabolites.
Patterns of daytime physical activity in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Actigraphy in PACE: 21% pervasively inactive, 11% pervasively active, 30% boom-and-bust, 38% indeterminate; inactive group more disabled, boom-bust more sleep disturbance.
nt: Oxford criteria CFS; baseline before treatment

t: Do adolescents with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS/ME) and co-morbid anxiety and/or depressive symptoms think differently to those who do not have co-morbid psychopathology?
f: Adolescents with CFS/ME and comorbid psychopathology endorsed more negative cognitive errors and catastrophising (d 0.5-1.3).

t: Systematic Review of the Epidemiological Burden of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome Across Europe: Current Evidence and EUROMENE Research Recommendations for Epidemiology.
f: European systematic review: ME/CFS prevalence 0.1-2.2% across scarce studies.

t: Paradigm shift to disequilibrium in the genesis of orthostatic intolerance in patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis and chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Disequilibrium (eyes-closed postural instability) in 32% and POT in 22% of ME patients; 26% failed the 10-min standing test, 89% of whom had disequilibrium.

t: Does Motor Cortex Engagement During Movement Preparation Differentially Inhibit Nociceptive Processing in Patients with Chronic Whiplash Associated Disorders, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome and Healthy Controls? An Experimental Study.
f: Movement-preparation attenuation of laser-evoked potentials was similar in CFS and controls, not supporting impaired motor-induced nociceptive inhibition.

t: Fallout from the COVID-19 pandemic - should we prepare for a tsunami of post viral depression?
f: Commentary on potential post-viral depression after COVID-19 and overlap with ME/CFS.

t: A systematic review of metabolomic dysregulation in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome/Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Systemic Exertion Intolerance Disease (CFS/ME/SEID).
f: Systematic review of blood and urine metabolomics found inconsistent results across 11 studies.

t: The feasibility and acceptability of an early intervention in primary care to prevent chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) in adults: randomised controlled trial.
Auricular acupuncture for insomnia of chronic fatigue syndrome: a case report.
The role of partners' fatigue and the patient-partner relationship in the outcome of cognitive behavioural therapy for chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Partners of CFS patients were less fatigued than controls; female partner fatigue and relationship dissatisfaction predicted CBT outcome.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome: help young people regain their lives.
A systematic review of neurological impairments in myalgic encephalomyelitis/ chronic fatigue syndrome using neuroimaging techniques.
f: Systematic review of neuroimaging: differences reported in grey and white matter volume, cerebral blood flow, EEG, connectivity, but heterogeneous.

t: Intravenous Cyclophosphamide in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome. An Open-Label Phase II Study.
Human Herpesvirus-6 Reactivation, Mitochondrial Fragmentation, and the Coordination of Antiviral and Metabolic Phenotypes in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
Altered muscle membrane potential and redox status differentiates two subgroups of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Resting and exercising muscle membrane excitability (M-wave) altered in 39 patients who also had higher oxidative stress markers and lower exercise K+ outflow; 33 patients had none, indicating subgroups.
nt: No healthy control group in abstract; at least four criteria

t: Unravelling myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS): Gender-specific changes in the microRNA expression profiling in ME/CFS.
f: PBMC miRNA expression after exercise differed by sex and nutritional status in ME/CFS.

t: The effect of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) severity on cellular bioenergetic function.
f: PBMC bioenergetics: both moderate and severe ME/CFS had reduced mitochondrial and ATP-linked respiration vs controls; severe had higher respiratory acidification and lower glycolysis once corrected.

f: Argues CBT evidence for reducing distress is weak and patient surveys report worsening.

f: Bias appraisal comparing a psychosocial trial (PACE) with a cellular study.

f: CFS had lower pressure pain thresholds (about 25% lower than MS) and higher temporal summation, indicating pain facilitation rather than impaired inhibition.

t: Vitamin and mineral status in chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
f: Vitamin E lower in patients (SMD -1.57) but not in high-quality studies; no consistent vitamin or mineral deficiency.

t: PACE trial authors continue to ignore their own null effect.
f: Commentary: PACE outcome changes inflated efficacy claims; no objective improvement.

t: Fecal metagenomic profiles in subgroups of patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.
Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and gulf war illness patients exhibit increased humoral responses to the herpesviruses-encoded dUTPase: Implications in disease pathophysiology.

f: Fewer than half had seen an ME/CFS specialist; 99% wanted specialist care.

t: Trends in the incidence of chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia in the UK, 2001-2013: a Clinical Practice Research Datalink study.

t: 'It feels sometimes like my house has burnt down, but I can see the sky': A qualitative study exploring patients' views of cognitive behavioural therapy for chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Patients reported satisfaction and partial improvement with CBT but incomplete recovery.

t: Long-term follow-up after cognitive behaviour therapy for chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Up to 10 years after CBT, fatigue and physical functioning had worsened since post-treatment; 37% had normal fatigue and 70% unimpaired function.

t: Characterization of a protein-bound polysaccharide from Herba Epimedii and its metabolic mechanism in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Epimedium polysaccharide altered urinary metabolites and two pathways in a rat CFS model.

t: Acupuncture and moxibustion for chronic fatigue syndrome in traditional Chinese medicine: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
f: Meta-analysis of Chinese RCTs: combined acupuncture plus moxibustion had higher total effective rate than herbal medicine or western medicine; evidence quality likely low.

t: Detection of Urine Metabolites in a Rat Model of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome before and after Exercise.

nt: Animal stress model, not human ME/CFS

t: Differences in ME and CFS Symptomology in Patients with Normal and Abnormal Exercise Test Results.
f: ME/CFS patients with abnormal exercise test results had more frequent and severe PEM, worse function and more bedbound status than those with normal results.

t: Do graded activity therapies cause harm in chronic fatigue syndrome?
f: Commentary arguing PACE safety data do not exclude harm from graded activity therapies, given poor fitness change (non-adherence) and patient reports of deterioration.

t: Activin B is a novel biomarker for chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (CFS/ME) diagnosis: a cross sectional study.
f: Serum activin B was elevated in CFS/ME vs controls and reference interval; activin A, follistatin and routine pathology were normal.
nt: Small, no n in abstract, not replicated

t: Clinically proven mtDNA mutations are not common in those with chronic fatigue syndrome.

f: Discussion paper comparing CBT for paediatric CFS/ME and depression.

t: Biological underpinnings of chronic fatigue syndrome begin to emerge.

n: 257 mixed (back pain, widespread pain, FM, ME/CFS)

t: Well-being in Chronic Fatigue Syndrome: Relationship to Symptoms and Psychological Distress.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome and the biopsychosocial model.

t: Differences in alexithymia and emotional awareness in exhaustion syndrome and chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: CFS had worse observer-rated emotional awareness and more difficulty identifying emotions than controls.

f: Lower putamen activity during low-reward condition in childhood CFS, correlated with fatigue severity.

t: Cognitive behavioural therapy in the treatment of chronic fatigue syndrome: A narrative review on efficacy and informed consent.

t: The utility of patient-reported outcome measures among patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.

t: Clinical assessment of the physical activity pattern of chronic fatigue syndrome patients: a validation of three methods.
f: Three activity-pattern instruments (API, IPAQ, CFS-AQ) had fair validity against actometers (AUC 0.64-0.71) with many misclassifications.

t: Functional characterization of muscle fibres from patients with chronic fatigue syndrome: case-control study.
f: Muscle biopsies showed a shift from slow to fast-twitch fibre proportion in CFS, with preserved single-fibre force, velocity and calcium sensitivity.

t: Associations between pet ownership and self-reported health status in people suffering from chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Pet ownership (58%) was not associated with fatigue, GHQ-12 or SF-36 scores.

t: Ventricular cerebrospinal fluid lactate is increased in chronic fatigue syndrome compared with generalized anxiety disorder: an in vivo 3.0 T (1)H MRS imaging study.
Cardiac function fluctuates during exacerbation and remission in young adults with chronic fatigue syndrome and "small heart".
f: Small heart on chest X-ray was common in CFS; echo showed small LV chamber and poor cardiac performance, which fluctuated with symptom severity across repeated exams.
nt: No control group in abstract; Fukuda-type criteria likely

t: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study of a probiotic in emotional symptoms of chronic fatigue syndrome.
Chronic fatigue syndrome and complement activation.
f: Case report: complement split products positive for 14 months in a post-EBV CFS patient, who then recovered.

t: Lower ambulatory blood pressure in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: 24-h ambulatory BP: CFS had lower systolic blood pressure and abnormal diurnal regulation vs controls, with a fatigue comparison group (PBC) included.

t: High court rejects challenge to NICE guidelines on chronic fatigue syndrome.
Premorbid personality in chronic fatigue syndrome as determined by the Temperament and Character Inventory.
f: Premorbid personality (TCI): lower novelty seeking, higher harm avoidance and persistence in CFS.

t: On the question of infectious aetiologies for multiple sclerosis, schizophrenia and the chronic fatigue syndrome and their treatment with antibiotics.
f: Open pilot of antibiotics for presumed Chlamydia pneumoniae infection in psychosis, with two CFS patients added; reports good outcomes.

t: Illness intrusiveness in myalgic encephalomyelitis: an exploratory study.
f: Illness intrusiveness correlated with fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, disability and depression in 24 ME patients.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome and the immune system: "findings in search of meanings".
Use of the Temperament and Character Inventory (TCI) for assessment of personality in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: CFS patients scored higher on harm avoidance and persistence (TCI).

t: Detection of herpesviruses and parvovirus B19 in gastric and intestinal mucosa of chronic fatigue syndrome patients.
f: Parvovirus B19 DNA found in gastric/intestinal biopsies in 40% of CFS vs <15% of controls; HHV-7 common in both; EBV and HHV-6 in 15-30%.
nt: Same gut-biopsy approach as Chia enterovirus work; unreplicated

t: Effects of the intelligent-turtle massage on the physical symptoms and immune functions in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
An investigation into the cognitive deficits associated with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Large CFS sample showed clear cognitive impairment on an extensive battery, independent of psychopathology.
nt: Sample size not given in abstract

t: Visible and near-infrared spectral changes in the thumb of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Vis-NIR spectroscopy of thumb: lower water, higher oxyhaemoglobin and more oxidised cytochrome c oxidase in CFS, read as faster blood flow and energy metabolism.
nt: Unvalidated technique, resting thumb only; finding opposes tissue under-perfusion

t: Can sustained arousal explain the Chronic Fatigue Syndrome?
Does hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis hypofunction in chronic fatigue syndrome reflect a 'crash' in the stress system?
f: Review hypothesising that HPA hypofunction in CFS reflects a dysregulated stress system with a cytokine-driven sickness response.

t: The lifestyle of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome and the effect on fatigue and functional impairments.
f: Lifestyle (smoking, diet, BMI) of CFS patients was no worse than the Dutch population on weight and alcohol; unhealthy factors were not associated with fatigue or impairment.

t: No apparent difference in the prevalence of parvovirus B19 infection between chronic fatigue syndrome patients and healthy controls in Japan.
Comparative epidemiology of chronic fatigue syndrome in Brazilian and British primary care: prevalence and recognition.
f: CDC-criteria prevalence 2.1% (London) vs 1.6% (Sao Paulo), p=0.20; diagnosed in 11 British cases but none in Brazil.

t: Review: CBT reduces fatigue in adults with chronic fatigue syndrome but effects at follow-up unclear.
[Somatic comorbidities in irritable bowel syndrome: fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue syndrome, and interstitial cystitis].
f: German review of fibromyalgia, CFS and interstitial cystitis overlap with IBS, proposing central hypersensitisation.

t: Effect of supplement with lactic-acid producing bacteria on fatigue and physical activity in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Four weeks of a multi-strain probiotic: no change in fatigue or activity; neurocognitive scores improved; gut flora unchanged; 6 of 15 reported improvement.

t: Practice Nurses' views of their role in the management of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome/Myalagic Encephalitis: a qualitative study.
f: Practice nurses had limited CFS/ME knowledge and some held sceptical views, a barrier to primary care management.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome and mitochondrial dysfunction.
f: Neutrophil "ATP profile" mitochondrial indices correlated with Bell scale severity (p<0.001); 70 of 71 patients outside the normal region.
nt: Commercial proprietary test, unclear methods, possible conflict of interest

t: Neuropsychological functioning, illness perception, mood and quality of life in chronic fatigue syndrome, autoimmune thyroid disease and healthy participants.
f: CFS group had impaired memory, attention and visuo-construction; attention deficit remained after controlling for mood.
n: 21 CFS vs 20 thyroid disease vs 21 healthy

t: Protective effects of antidepressants against chronic fatigue syndrome-induced behavioral changes and biochemical alterations.

Serial structural MRI analysis and proton and 31PMR spectroscopy in the investigation of cerebral fatty acids in major depressive disorder, Huntington's disease, myalgic encephalomyelitis and in forensic schizophrenic patients.
B-CELL DEPLETING AGENTS, LIKE ANTI-CD20 ANTIBODIES OR FRAGMENTS THEREOF FOR THE TREATMENT OF CHRONIC FATIGUE SYNDROME
f: Patent application for anti-CD20 antibodies in CFS/ME; no data.

t: Why myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) may kill you: disorders in the inflammatory and oxidative and nitrosative stress (IO&NS) pathways may explain cardiovascular disorders in ME/CFS.

f: Plasma CoQ10 significantly lower in ME/CFS (p=0.00001); 44.8% below the lowest control value; inversely related to fatigue and autonomic symptom scores.
nt: Plasma CoQ10 deficiency not in atlas; unreplicated; speculative mortality claims

t: Kindling and Oxidative Stress as Contributors to Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.
f: Hypothesis paper proposing kindling and oxidative stress as unifying mechanisms.

t: A review on cognitive behavorial therapy (CBT) and graded exercise therapy (GET) in myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME) / chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS): CBT/GET is not only ineffective and not evidence-based, but also potentially harmful for many patients with ME/CFS.
Increased 8-hydroxy-deoxyguanosine, a marker of oxidative damage to DNA, in major depression and myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Urinary 8-OHdG (creatinine-adjusted) was higher in patients with both depression and ME/CFS than controls and other groups; correlated with FF scale.
nt: ME/CFS alone not elevated per abstract; urine marker

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome: la bête noire of the Belgian health care system.

"Functional" or "psychosomatic" symptoms, e.g. a flu-like malaise, aches and pain and fatigue, are major features of major and in particular of melancholic depression.
f: Fatigue and somatic symptoms in depression form a dimension separate from the depression factor.

t: Anticardiolipin antibodies in the sera of patients with diagnosed chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: IgM anticardiolipin antibodies found in 95% of CFS sera.
nt: No control numbers in abstract; unreplicated

t: Childhood trauma and risk for chronic fatigue syndrome: association with neuroendocrine dysfunction.
f: Childhood trauma associated with 6-fold increased CFS risk; low salivary cortisol response to awakening found only in a CFS subgroup with trauma.

t: The doctor-patient relationship in chronic fatigue syndrome: survey of patient perspectives.
Women with chronic fatigue syndrome and sexual dysfunction: past, present, and future.
f: Short review noting sexual dysfunction (low desire) in women with CFS and scarce data.

t: [Chronic fatigue syndrome: a psychoneuroimmunological perspective].
The role of coping in the relationship between depression and illness severity in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: About 70% of patients were moderately or severely depressed; coping styles related to appraisals of illness severity.

t: A Bayesian approach to gene-gene and gene-environment interactions in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Bayesian analysis of CDC SNP data found NR3C1 in significant gene-gene and gene-gender interaction models.
nt: Reanalysis of old candidate-gene data; no replication

t: [Experience of application of adaptol in treatment of chronic fatigue syndrome in patients with chronic cerebral ischemia].
Physiological cost of walking in those with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS): a case-control study.
f: Walking at preferred speed was slower in CFS (0.84 vs 1.19 m/s) and the physiological (oxygen) cost of walking was higher than controls.

t: Are chronic fatigue and chronic fatigue syndrome valid clinical entities across countries and health-care settings?

[Reaction on 'Chronic fatigue syndrome: a psychoneuroimmunological perspective' (2)].
Exploring the beliefs and underlying functional deficits associated with chronic fatigue syndrome and the identification of predictors of recovery and successful illness management
f: Thesis description on beliefs, deficits and predictors of recovery; no results in abstract.

t: ~I had to give up so, so much~ : a narrative study to investigate the impact of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS) on the lives of young people
Treatment of chronic fatigue syndrome: findings, principles and strategies.
Secondary structural changes of proteins in fingernails of chronic fatigue syndrome patients from Fourier-transform infrared spectra.
f: FTIR of fingernails showed lower alpha-helix and higher beta-sheet protein content in CFS.
nt: Unreplicated exploratory technique (same Japanese group as thumb Vis-NIR)

t: Longitudinal change in chronic fatigue syndrome: what home-based assessments reveal.
f: Over 2 years, self-reported improvement tracked with momentary fatigue and standing time; actigraphy change correlated with physical function; <20% reached healthy range.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis (or encephalopathy).
f: NICE 2007 guideline CG53 on diagnosis and management of CFS/ME (later replaced by NG206).

t: Astragalus membranaceus flavonoids (AMF) ameliorate chronic fatigue syndrome induced by food intake restriction plus forced swimming.
Gene profiling of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis.
f: Review of microarray work: 88 differentially expressed genes (85 up); qPCR clustering gave seven subtypes with different SF-36 scores and severity.
nt: Reviews the authors' own earlier work; unreplicated

t: Deficits of interference control in adolescents with chronic fatigue syndrome.

t: Clinical observation on the effects of Bo's abdominal acupuncture in 40 cases of chronic fatigue syndrome.

nt: Very small sample; opposite baseline direction to Jammes 2009 (low Hsp70)

t: Normalization of leaky gut in chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) is accompanied by a clinical improvement: effects of age, duration of illness and the translocation of LPS from gram-negative bacteria.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome and DSM-IV personality disorders.

t: Does depression mediate the relation between fatigue severity and disability in chronic fatigue syndrome sufferers?
f: Depression mediated the fatigue-disability relationship in CFS.

t: Memory and attention problems in children with chronic fatigue syndrome or myalgic encephalopathy.
f: Children with CFS/ME scored below norms on sustained, switching and divided attention and auditory learning.

t: Association between school absence and physical function in paediatric chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalopathy.

t: A role for the body burden of aluminium in vaccine-associated macrophagic myofasciitis and chronic fatigue syndrome.
Transcriptional control of complement activation in an exercise model of chronic fatigue syndrome.
Integrated weighted gene co-expression network analysis with an application to chronic fatigue syndrome.

nt: Methods paper on CDC microarray data; no external validation of biology

t: Vaccination as teenagers against meningococcal disease and the risk of the chronic fatigue syndrome.

t: Contact lens-related acanthamoeba keratitis in a patient with chronic fatigue syndrome.
Customizing treatment of chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia: the role of perpetuating factors.

t: Prevalence of chronic widespread pain and chronic fatigue syndrome in Korean livestock raisers.

t: Are patients with chronic fatigue syndrome just 'tired' or also 'sleepy'?
f: MSLT sleep latency was shorter in CFS than controls but within normal range; CFS had less objective sleepiness than sleep apnoea and higher fatigue.

t: A train-the-trainer education and promotion program: chronic fatigue syndrome--a diagnostic and management challenge.
f: US train-the-trainer education program reached 2064 primary care providers.

t: Factors associated with depression among individuals with chronic fatigue syndrome: findings from a nationally representative survey.
f: 36% of self-reported CFS respondents were depressed; 22% of depressed had considered suicide.

t: Cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic fatigue syndrome.
Anaesthesia for patients with idiopathic environmental intolerance and chronic fatigue syndrome.
Guided self-instructions for people with chronic fatigue syndrome: randomised controlled trial.
Neuroendocrine and immune network re-modeling in chronic fatigue syndrome: an exploratory analysis.
f: Network analysis integrating gene expression and neuroendocrine data showed rewiring around pituitary and thyroid nodes in CFS.

t: Assessment of fibromyalgia & chronic fatigue syndrome: a new protocol designed to determine work capability--chronic pain abilities determination (CPAD).

f: Blood microarray: CD19+ B-cell gene set lower in CFS (p=0.01; PTPRK, TSPAN3); co-expression suggested inflammatory signalling.

t: Psychomotor functioning in chronic fatigue syndrome and major depressive disorder: a comparative study.
f: Both CFS and MDD patients had fine motor slowing vs controls on copying tasks.

t: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome is an under-recognized condition in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Active stand test: max heart rate higher in CFS/ME (106 vs 98 bpm, p=0.02); POTS in 27% (16/59) vs 9% of controls (p=0.006).

t: Immunological aspects of chronic fatigue syndrome.
Hypothesis: chronic fatigue syndrome is caused by dysregulation of hydrogen sulfide metabolism.
Chronic fatigue syndrome: a hormonal origin? A rare case of dysmenorrhea membranacea.
Lower frequency of IL-17F sequence variant (His161Arg) in chronic fatigue syndrome patients.
f: Lower frequency of the IL-17F His161Arg (rs763780 C) allele in CFS patients vs controls.

t: Functional incapacity and physical and psychological symptoms: how they interconnect in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Principal components separated psychological symptoms from a physical-symptom/functioning/fatigue component; functional incapacity tracked physical symptoms.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome and the central nervous system.
Identification of marker genes for differential diagnosis of chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Nine-gene blood expression set (incl. GZMA, ATP5J2, COX5B, STAT5A) classified 94% of CFS and 92% of non-CFS fatigue patients in a final PCR set.

nt: Small, no independent replication, classifier optimism

t: HPA-axis dysfunction in chronic fatigue syndrome: clinical implications.

t: Kinesiophobia and symptomatology in chronic fatigue syndrome: a psychometric study of two questionnaires.
f: Dutch and French kinesiophobia and symptom list questionnaires showed good reliability.

t: Nitric oxide modulation mediates the protective effect of trazodone in a mouse model of chronic fatigue syndrome.
Can CBT substantially change grey matter volume in chronic fatigue syndrome?
Chronic fatigue syndrome with autoantibodies--the result of an augmented adjuvant effect of hepatitis-B vaccine and silicone implant.
Implementing cognitive behavior therapy for chronic fatigue syndrome in mental health care: a costs and outcomes analysis.
f: Implemented CBT: 37% recovered; costs fell and the programme was cost-saving from a societal view.

t: Pilot study of peripheral muscle function in primary biliary cirrhosis: potential implications for fatigue pathogenesis.
f: 31P-MRS during low-intensity exercise: ADP-PCr recovery kinetics were normal in CFS/ME (mitochondrial regulation intact), but lost in primary biliary cirrhosis.
nt: CFS/ME is only the fatigued comparator, n=8

t: Increased oxidative stress suggested by low serum vitamin E concentrations in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
Prefrontal cortex oxygenation during incremental exercise in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: During incremental exercise, CFS reached exhaustion sooner (351 vs 715 s) with lower prefrontal oxygenation (HbO2, HHb, tHb, TOI) and lower max HR.

t: Post-radiation syndrome as a NO/ONOO- cycle, chronic fatigue syndrome-like disease.
f: Proposes post-radiation syndrome as an NO/ONOO- cycle CFS-like illness.

t: Application of Chinese medicinal composition in preparing medicament for treating chronic fatigue syndrome
Cognitive behaviour therapy for chronic fatigue syndrome in adults.
f: Cochrane review: CBT vs usual care reduced fatigue (SMD -0.39, 95% CI -0.60 to -0.19; 6 studies, 373 participants).
nt: Subjective outcomes, unblinded trials, Oxford/Fukuda populations

t: Diffuse noxious inhibitory control is delayed in chronic fatigue syndrome: an experimental study.
Neuropsychological performance in persons with chronic fatigue syndrome: results from a population-based study.
f: CANTAB: CFS had slower motor speed and impaired spatial working memory and recognition versus controls after excluding psychiatric disorders and cognitive drugs.

t: Small heart syndrome in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: A considerable number of CFS patients had a small heart on chest X-ray (cardiothoracic ratio).

t: Using multiple sources of knowledge to reach clinical understanding of chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Interviews show physicians draw on social and cultural knowledge to understand CFS/ME.

t: Attentional bias towards health-threat information in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: CFS group showed attentional bias to health-threat stimuli.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome: implications for women and their health care providers during the childbearing years.
Increase in prefrontal cortical volume following cognitive behavioural therapy in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: At baseline CFS had lower grey matter volume; after CBT grey matter increased in lateral prefrontal cortex, related to cognitive speed.
nt: Small; atlas notes no consistent structural MRI difference; no untreated control follow-up in abstract

t: Glucocorticoid receptor mediated negative feedback in chronic fatigue syndrome using the low dose (0.5 mg) dexamethasone suppression test.
f: Low-dose dexamethasone suppression: basal cortisol was raised and overall suppression did not differ (80% vs 76%); only the comorbid-depression subgroup (n=9) hypersuppressed.

t: Curcumin, a polyphenolic antioxidant, attenuates chronic fatigue syndrome in murine water immersion stress model.
Diagnostic and treatment challenges of chronic fatigue syndrome: role of immediate-release methylphenidate.

An IgM-mediated immune response directed against nitro-bovine serum albumin (nitro-BSA) in chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) and major depression: evidence that nitrosative stress is another factor underpinning the comorbidity between major depression and CFS.
f: Serum IgM to nitro-BSA was higher in CFS, partial CFS and MDD than controls (highest in CFS) and correlated with IgM/IgA to gut-bacteria LPS.

t: Gait characteristics of subjects with chronic fatigue syndrome and controls at self-selected and matched velocities.
f: Over-ground gait differed in CFS at self-selected speed (slower, p=0.002); when speed matched, patterns similar except at the ankles.

t: Determinants of health care use in chronic fatigue syndrome patients: a cross-sectional study.
f: Health care use in CFS was predicted by fatigue and perpetuating beliefs such as symptom focus; tertiary patients used more specialist care.

t: Obstructions for quality care experienced by patients with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS)--a case study.
f: Patients reported disbelief, psychologising by doctors and worsening with prescribed activity.

t: Sleep structure and sleepiness in chronic fatigue syndrome with or without coexisting fibromyalgia.
f: Polysomnography: CFS had less total sleep, lower efficiency and less REM than controls; unrefreshing sleep linked to poor sleep efficiency and short sleep runs.

t: The Energy Envelope Theory and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Higher daily energy quotient (expended/perceived energy) was associated with worse fatigue, pain, depression, QoL and disability.

t: Preexisting psychological stress predicts acute and chronic fatigue and arthritis following symptomatic parvovirus B19 infection.
f: High pre-infection stress index predicted CFS/ME 1-3 years after symptomatic parvovirus B19 (OR 25.7, 1.7-121.9).

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome in male Gulf war veterans and civilians: a further test of the single syndrome hypothesis.
Can exercise limits prevent post-exertional malaise in chronic fatigue syndrome? An uncontrolled clinical trial.
f: Walk limited by heart rate at RER 1.0 raised fatigue immediately that returned to baseline at 24 h; pain stayed elevated; 6 of 24 felt worse.

t: Comorbid somatic symptoms and functional status in patients with fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome: sensory amplification as a common mechanism.
f: Sensory amplification related to physical functioning via pain intensity, independent of depression.

t: The neural correlates of fatigue: an exploratory imaginal fatigue provocation study in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: fMRI during imagined fatigue: CFS had more occipito-parietal/posterior cingulate and less prefrontal activation than controls; reverse pattern with anxiety scenarios.

t: Is chronic fatigue syndrome caused by a rare brain infection of a common, normally benign virus?
f: Hypothesis that CFS is caused by a circovirus entering the brain.

t: Dynamics of sleep stage transitions in healthy humans and patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Polysomnography transition statistics: fewer REM-to-non-REM transitions and more REM/stage-I-to-wake transitions in CFS.

t: The economic impact of ME/CFS: individual and societal costs.
f: Estimated annual direct cost per patient of $2,342 (community) and $8,675 (tertiary); total cost to US society about $18.7-24 billion.

t: Gene expression subtypes in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis.
f: 88 genes differentially expressed in blood (85 up); qPCR clustering gave 7 subtypes with different SF-36 scores and severity.

t: The awareness of chronic fatigue syndrome: a comparative study in Brazil and the United Kingdom.
f: Awareness of CFS was 16.2% in Brazilian vs 55.1% in British primary care attenders; 30.8% of Brazilian specialists named CFS for a vignette.

t: Dietary intervention in chronic fatigue syndrome.
Low-grade inflammation and arterial wave reflection in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Arterial stiffness (AIx@75) was greater in CFS (22.5 vs 13.3%, p=0.002), with higher CRP and isoprostanes, correlating with CRP and oxidative stress.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome: an approach combining self-management with graded exercise to avoid exacerbations.
f: Narrative argues graded exercise with self-management and pacing can be done safely without immune harm.

t: Etiology of chronic fatigue syndrome: testing popular hypotheses using a national birth cohort study.
f: Prospective cohort: CFS (1.1%) was not preceded by more childhood illness or atopy; higher childhood/adult exercise frequency and lower BMI preceded later CFS.

t: Alterations in diurnal salivary cortisol rhythm in a population-based sample of cases with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Flattened diurnal cortisol: lower morning and higher evening salivary cortisol in CFS; IL-6 highest in CFS but not significant after BMI adjustment.

Brain atrophy in a murine model of chronic fatigue syndrome and beneficial effect of Hochu-ekki-to (TJ-41).
Intracellular immune dysfunction in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome: state of the art and therapeutic implications.
Breathing retraining in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome: a pilot study.

t: Health-related quality of life in chronic fatigue syndrome: predictors of physical functioning and psychological distress.
f: HRQoL much lower than norms; 63% had clinically significant psychological distress; physical fatigue and symptom frequency best predictors.

t: Efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy for adolescents with chronic fatigue syndrome: long-term follow-up of a randomized, controlled trial.
f: 2.1-year follow-up of CBT RCT: fatigue gains maintained; physical function and school attendance rose further.

t: Traditional chinese medicine for chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Narrative review of traditional Chinese medicine for CFS; no pooled data.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome defies the mind-body-schism of medicine. New perspectives on a multiple realisable developmental systems disorder.

t: Effectiveness of distant healing for patients with chronic fatigue syndrome: a randomised controlled partially blinded trial (EUHEALS).
Possible role for early-life immune insult including developmental immunotoxicity in chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) or myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME).
A precarious balance: using a self-regulation model to conceptualize and treat chronic fatigue syndrome.
Genetic evaluation of the serotonergic system in chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Three HTR2A polymorphisms (-1438G/A, C102T, rs1923884) associated with CFS and with disability and fatigue measures.

A matched case control study of orthostatic intolerance in children/adolescents with chronic fatigue syndrome.
f: Head-up tilt: orthostatic intolerance in 13 CFS vs 5 controls; POTS without hypotension in 7 CFS and no controls; sympathetic predominance in HRV.

t: Implementing cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic fatigue syndrome in a mental health center: a benchmarking evaluation.
f: Implemented CBT had effect sizes comparable to RCTs, 32% early dropout.

t: A longitudinal study of the relationship between psychological distress and recurrence of upper respiratory tract infections in chronic fatigue syndrome.

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome in children aged 11 years old and younger.

t: Anti-CD20 antibodies or fragments thereof for the treatment of chronic fatigue syndrome
f: Patent for anti-CD20 antibodies in CFS; no data.

t: Individuals' experience of chronic fatigue syndrome/myalgic encephalomyelitis: an interpretative phenomenological analysis.
f: IPA of interviews identified six themes on symptom perception and diagnosis.

t: Symptoms, impairment and illness intrusiveness--their relationship with depression in women with CFS/ME.

t: Neuroaetiology of chronic fatigue syndrome: an overview.

f: Thesis on illness cognitions of significant others of CFS patients; no results in abstract.

t: [Sub-health state and chronic fatigue syndrome].

t: Association of chronic fatigue syndrome and acute psychotic episode: is it coincidental?

t: Chronic fatigue syndrome: characteristics and possible causes for its pathogenesis.

t: Psychological factors in social relationships and home functioning of patients with chronic fatigue syndrome
f: Thesis on emotional expressivity and attitudes in relation to social and home functioning.

t: The associations between basal salivary cortisol and illness symptomatology in chronic fatigue syndrome.

t: Women's experiences of increasing subjective well-being in CFS/ME through leisure-based arts and crafts activities: a qualitative study.

t: Central nervous system abnormalities in fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome: new concepts in treatment.

t: [Risk factors for ischemic heart disease in patients with chronic fatigue syndrome].
